review:

look at that one star in the review and think zero stars. don't be real sick because if you are pick a different place than the hunters creek loop advent centra care.

it's the flu season and with the whole coronavirus situation, we showed up with face masks. but we didn't have any kids size masks and dr mathurs staff actually gave us one during our visit, my daughter dropped it by accident so we went to the front desk and ask for one. the lady asked if my baby has any flu like symptoms and i said no just for precautions. with her sh*t face acting like we were there to steal, she said it's only for anyone who has a flu. ok, i understand so i said thanks and went back to our seats. 

this ugly lowlife is clearly against us asians with face masks. because when the nurse called my daughter, me and my mom got up to head over. the ugly nasty lowlife dare to yelled at my mom to not come along. she yelled not once, not twice but three times. my mom doesn't speak english, by the time i turned around bitch got up from her seat and screamed so loud the whole lobby and surrounding office staff and patients looked over. her reason was theres no space for my mom. bitch there's an other person also in the lab, and her family is standing right by the door! if they can stand there, why can't my mom stand right outside just like other patients families. 

i just wanted to tell her to go to hell if my daughter weren't there with us. how can anyone so  be still living in this society. 

the whole check-in experience was terrible from start to finish. fire her already.

if i could give this place zero stars i would. the first time i went was when i broke my ankle. made us wait over four hours just to get an x-ray and we had to share a room with another patient. the next time was even worse. my girlfriend came in with abdominal pains and they made us wait three hours just to see a doctor. the doctor than told her she needed an ultrasound, which we waited two hours for and than another two for the results. after that they made her get a cat scan, which took up another two hours to get and another two for the results. than after all this doctor mchue came in for no more than thirty seconds to tell her nothing was wrong. they definitely just added procedures in order to rack up her hospital bill bordering on malpractice considering how much radiation a cat scan gives. after all this we had to wait another hour just so a nurse could come in for five seconds to take out her iv. when i went to complain to dr mchue, and told him we'd been at the hospital for almost 12 hours and we just need the iv to be taken out so we could go home, he rudely told me "people are dying." i understand that it's an emergency room but there were atleast ten people talking or sitting at their computers, one of which is capable of removing an iv, or dr mchue should've just done it himself when he came to see us. his attitude was not one any dr should have and it was clear he got stuck with the graveyard shift and was not happy about it. terrible terrible doctor. don't go unless you're literally dying because they will not help you. go to a different hospital if you can and definitely hope to god you don't get dr mchue, because i've never encountered a more rude or dismissive dr in my life. fuck this p

i will say, i haven't received my bill yet which i'm slightly nervous for - but i trust they'll have a great billing department. we were on vacation in wa when we were transported by ambulance to tacoma children's hospital. from the er to the last day we were here people were amazing. my daughter was have severe trouble breathing due to a severe case of croup, virus and bacterial infection. they were fast and efficient about getting her started on the meds she needed right away. dr. mccabe & dr. williams were the ones who were assigned to us, they were absolutely amazing! after thinking about it, i was so happy that we were in wa when this happened and not at our home (ca). because i can guarantee the care we received wouldn't have been able to compare to out in la.

it's never fun when you end up in the er. check in ran smoothly, but of a wait since lots of sick kiddos but it's that time of year with the flu and all. very grateful that people were wearing their face masks and all. 

once i got a bed it went pretty quickly, had my xrays and meds and the cool app that tells you the progress of the tests was so awesome! i really do like that new feature. 

but the bad happened as i was leaving :( i was given a  hospital gown to wear because i had a lot of x rays to take,  i mean i sprained my entire body from the fall i had. miracle i didn't break anything. anyway, the hospital gown had dry blood in the inside. i was not bleeding so this grossed me out  and my husband. immediately told the doctor and my nurse. they just said they'd wash it again, my husband said  they should throw it away. i was too drugged on percocet and muscle relaxers to argue. 

other than that i'm healing and feel better.  i do wish that the tree given to me at the end with my diagnosis was just given to me via  a link in that cool  app.

this hospital is hamstrung by its own policies. they cannot logically solve problems that require a creative solution.  my wife broke her jaw in a fall &  required a maxillo-facial surgeon to examine her. my wife & i just spent 7 hours in the er before the methodist personnel figured out there was no specialist to see her at this hospital. rather than giving us a referral to an appropriate specialist, their policy required us to go to another er in their system ( we are now in our 2nd er getting exposed to another environment filled with viruses and other potential sources of infection)

review: i'm in my late 40s. i am a former soldier. i have been to emergency rooms around the world. i was a paramedic for years. this was the wooooorst medical experience i have ever had. i have had my face reconstructed. i have been shot. i was unfortunate enough to experience the worse pain i have ever had in my life for the second time, another kidney stone. i knew exactly what it was. i told these assholes exactly what it was. i'm have insurance out the whazoo. but yet, these assholes let me roll around their nasty ass floor in pain for hours without once attempting to manage my pain. i didn't want any narcotics. i wanted toradol to open my vessels. i walked out twice because they refused to move with any sense of urgency to get me relief. listen to what i said, i walked out twice because they were disinterested in helping me in my severe distress. like i wanted to be in the emergency... i should not have been in this emergency room thinking i should shoot myself to get more expedited care. i didn't go through with it because they still probably wouldn't give me the toradol.... i walked out in severe pain, went to north richland hills emergency room, was in a bed in 10 minutes, got a shot of toradol in another 15 minutes, and past the stone in my urine sample within the hour...i pray to the lord that something replaces the triage nurse and doctor in harris methodist er, to include the corona virus.

i wasnt feeling well so my husband took me to the emergency room.  it was busy and we waited for about 5 hours. when i got to my room in the er the doctor was very blunt and to the point, almost on the verge of rude. but shelby my nurse was amazing! so sweet and funny, she really did make it easier.  my blood test was off so her ordered an ultrasound and a ct scan. those were done right away and about an hour after shelby came in to start an iv line. i asked why and she said oh because you're having surgery soon, didnt the doctor come in and tell you? ummm no he didnt! when i got admitted and they were about to take me to my room he literally popped his head in and said "i'm sure you know by now that you're having surgery.  your gallbladder is not doing great so it needs to be removed." oh ok thanks. worst bedside manner ever. 
they got me to my room, and i understand that it's not a hotel and we cant really pick and choose, but they put me in with an elderly lady who had pneumonia and some other things going on and was highly contagious.  why would you put someone who is healthy and about to have surgery in with someone who is super sick?! i had some stuff going on with me that caused me to be quarantined so they ended up moving her. my husband asked if they could have someone come in and clean the bathroom since she was up and about all over the room and they said sure. nobody ever came and we ended up doing it ourselves (good thing there were purple wipes outside my door!) 
we were originally told that i was scheduled for surgery first thing in the morning, then my surgeon came in and said it would be around 10am. that was the last we heard all day. we kept asking when they would be taking me in and nobody had a clue. the lack of communication was phenomenal.  i ended up being the last surgery of the day because apparently my surgeon is a pushover and others kept pushing us back since they knew he wouldn't get mad.(my nurses words not mine.) meanwhile i got to sit in extreme pain not being able to eat or drink. not even water. after surgery i wasnt feeling too great and i asked for pain meds at midnight. i didnt get them until 4am. horrible. i had to beg for one of those sponges to wet my lips because i still wasnt allowed to eat or drink and when the aide finally said yes he watched me like i was a criminal to make sure i didnt drink any water. horrible. i waited until 9pm the next day for the dr to come in and see me and he ordered an mri for the next morning. they took me at about 745am and that went fine...until they left me in the hallway for 45 minutes after the mri! the tech walked by and i asked if they were going to take me back and he said "oh they haven't taken you back yet?" hmmm...wow! there were other things that happened but i will leave it at that for now. this was by far the worst experience i have ever had here. i strongly recommend going somewhere else if you need any services(other than having a baby...in that respect they're pretty awesome). only reason for two stars is because the nurses i had were really nice.

what has happened to this hospital??  my husband has been here many times, and most visits were good, except for the extremely long waits in the er.  my husband had surgery on friday and stayed overnight.  he just finished chemotherapy, so his immune system has been wiped out.  they obviously didn't consider this at all, or didn't care; so they gave him a room in the old wing where more than half the patients in the unit were quarantined!!  there were warning signs on the doors, but the doors were left open, so germs and bacteria could freely travel throughout the ward.  the nurses were unfriendly and unattentive.  my husband had to go looking for his nurse, pat, twice, and found her visiting in the corridor.  he was released by the surgeon the morning after surgery, but it took several hours for the nurses to complete the paperwork.  he was given no breakfast, and no explanation, even though it was allowed.  he was told he would be given lunch before leaving, and he had to ask about it three times before he was finally given a tray.  his "lunch" was an omelet full of eggshells!  obviously someone's breakfast that they didn't want.  he was in excrutiating pain, but they refused to give him pain medication because the doctor's orders had already been written.  he told the nurse how severe his pain was, and instead of offering to call the doctor for permission to dispense more pain medication, she asked if she should call the doctor for permission to stay in the hospital another night, knowing that no one would volunteer to stay one more night in that terrible situation.  we are very upset and disappointed that the hospital has changed so drastically.  i see from the other reviews that this experience was not a one-time exception; it has become the norm.

i have already placed a call to hospital administration to make them aware of the subpar treatment we received, but i also want to make certain the public is aware as well. please do  not waste your time at this emergency dept. i highly recommend going to savannah as we should have done, but our son was very sick so we stopped here rather than proceeding to savannah. he had been diagnosed w type b flu on monday. our doctor encouraged us to return or take him to an er/urgent care if after hours if he became worse. in the early morning hours of wednesday he became much worse; screaming in pain, unable to feel his legs below the knees, and a spike in fever despite tylenol  & motrin, and began vomiting. we rushed him to coastal carolina er.  from the second we stepped in the door the treatment we received was inexcusable. the check in person yelled across the room to ask what was wrong as we were struggling to get him in the door. i explained
he had been diagnosed w flu earlier in the week & she simply threw a mask at me rather than offering some help to get him in. the triage nurse was hateful and also offered no help.  she put us in a cold room w no sheet or blanket on the bed and left. we were then greeted by an extremely hateful  dr sutherland who asked why we were there. we explained what was going on, his diagnosis, & then she asked what we expected her to do as this was common for the flu.  we explained our doctor told us to immediately have him seen if he became worse which he did, which is why we were there.  she looked at me & left the room. the triage nurse returns, does not bother to tell us what she's giving him until i ask. she gives him zofran and tylenol/motrin & leaves. my son was absolutely freezing so i walk to nurses desk to ask for a blanket & hear them discussing the fact of how ridiculous they think it is that we brought our son to the er. (i am fairly certain this is a hippaa violation...we have contacted the governing board as well). she snaps at me that she's "fixin  to discharge him" (her exact words) so a blanket wont be necessary.  i realize it was nearing the 7am shift change  but this lack of care our  son received is completely inexcusable. we will never return to this facility and will discourage anyone from visiting this er.

review:

get back in the room and was first seen by a student doctor i think he was. he actually was asking questions . then he got the attending doctor. he basically came in later and said it could be one of three things scarlet fever ,mono which she was kind of young for or an allergic reaction to the amoxicillin. then he got the head of the er when she came in she basically said that it was a virus and that's why she had a rash. she didn't say what kind of virus what could've caused the virus nothing. they said they were going to give her some benadryl and watch her and then write her a prescription for zyrtec. it took the nurse a while to even give her the benadryl. when the medical student came back in at first he said it was looking better and then said let me get the doctor.then the attending doctor came back in and said they're not blowing this off don't think that if it was his child he would be fine with sending sending them home. i asked him if it will be cleared up for monday because review: brought my mom is a few months ago (before the coronavirus) because she couldn't regulate her temperature due to her cancer treatments. the nurse kept saying we were safer to stay home. i get it! we are surrounded by sick people but she was covered in blankets and heating pads and felt like she was going to freeze. when she finally got a room days later the nurse was more concerned about the paperwork than my mom. she asked us the same questions we already answered three times before about her medications and medical history. mom started to get chills again which is always followed by a high fever. i told her and that tylenol would do the trick. she wouldn't give it to her bc the fever hadn't spiked yet. it's just tylenol!!! she kept asking her questions but by then my mom was delirious and couldn't even say her own name! she kept saying she was fine and just tired. i begged for tylenol but they refused. they used the external temperature and it was 99. they said they will wait till it got to 100 to give her tylenol. i brought my own oral thermometer and it read 102. finally i had to call the head nurse to get help and by then her fever was 103!!!! this is the worst place! i hope that nurse gets fired!!! they had no regard for my moms well being and we will never go there again.

my grandfather went in a normal functioning senior when i brought him to the er to have fluid drained from his lung. we were moved to the third-floor until they could do the procedure (we were told we would be called before they took him in so we could be there when he woke up) they never called. they didn't call before hand and they didn't call when he came out of surgery either. he was heavily medicated with morphine. when we arrived to the hospital he was  restricted to the bed with restraints on his hands and legs. he was combative due to the anesthesia and morphine. he was sedated all day and would start to come back to life at night, hungry, wanting to get up, wanting answers as to where he was, he was very confused, he would start to get upset and they would sedate him because he would start to get combative, this lasted for three days. i had to stay in the hospital with him over night to insure they wouldn't sedate him again. it was crazy to me that the second a patient would get upset they would sedate him. i was told several times oh he's old....this is how how old people act...they thought he had dementia. i kept explaining no, he doesn't act like this..it's something else...it's the medication you're giving him. go to find out they are giving him anti psychotics looking into it further he had every side effect of the antipsychotic medication they were giving him which was making him behave that way. i felt like i couldn't leave him at the hospital alone because i was worried he would be mistreated. from that first day of coming out of surgery he was labeled as a hazard a threat to himself and a threat to others that followed him throughout his two week stay at the hospital even though that had only lasted those first three days due to the medication that was being given to him once we order doctors and nurses not to give him the antipsychotic drug everything started to subside  long story short the part of my complaint is this- my grandfather was moved from five different rooms five different floors. i would ask a question the nurses would say oh this is at my floor i don't know. five different doctors all telling us different information and ordering different medication. nurses coming in at all hours of the night being super loud with no intention of really doing anything just basically coming in and being disruptive and result waking him up when he finally goes to sleep. the 5th floor in the north tower was awful. once he was on that floor no one could be bothered with him. and when it was time for discharge they said his ambulance would arrive at 5, 5 turned into 530, 530 turned into 6, 6 turned into 7, 7 turned into 8, 8 turned into 9. we said this is ridiculous and we're not gonna send a sleeping man to a rehabilitation that he's never been to before when he's having short-term memory confusion at 9 o'clock at night it will only confuse him and upset him not to mention it's 9 at night and i have to get home to my family myself, i didn't want him arriving alone... just send him tomorrow..they said no you have to leave the doctors already ordered the discharge and said there was nothing they could do about it and forced him to leave. totally unexceptionable in my opinion. no one ever checked his chart and would always ask what floor he came from, what did he have done...and so on. no one ever knew what was going on. too many doctors taking care of one person. none of them were on the same page . the third floor was the only decent part of this experience, we had one nurse named christina and review:
to sum it up - yikes. 

went  to the er on thursday after class for severe lower back pain that extended into my legs. 
the moment i got there, the triage nurse quarantined me out of suspect of corona virus. mind you, their only basis was that i had a fever (which i didn't even realize i had) and i am a japanese american. no other symptoms. they had someone come up to me every 5min (often the same person) to ask me the same questions (did you travel  abroad in the last 30 days; do you have a cough?) as if they would get a different answer. my answer was a hard no  each time. meanwhile i was in severe pain, and my chief complaint was not addressed until several hours  later. 

after a couple hours waiting in a quarantine area, they took me to what i thought would only be temporary accommodation. it was a patient bed  in a cramped hallway, and the bed was too short for my legs. it turned out to be the only patient bed i'd see in that hospital. pretty sure that was a major hipaa violation. 

my first nurse was absolutely atrocious. he did not smile. he was rude. he was in no way gentle. he missed my vein 4 times when placing an iv, which judging by the vein he  used, did not seem possible. when i had to give a urine sample, he made me hold my urine specimen for 20 min until another nurse came by and asked me why i was still holding it, and then he would not help me back into my  bed. i was in so much pain. the icing on the cake: he gave me a flu test and jammed the stick so far up my nose that i got a nose bleed. i didn't even know i had a nose bleed until the mri tech took off my mask and asked me why it was bleeding. after i told him, he shook it off as no big deal. i've had a couple flu test before -- none of which caused this much discomfort. 

at the end of the day, the docs couldn't figure out the root of my pain and gave me a referral to a spine specialist. they didn't give me a number -- the told me to wait for his call the next day. the specialist waited until the end of their business day to call me to schedule an appointment. i missed their call but called back not even 10min after their initial call. and they were already closed! i had to wait until monday (today) to try to book an appointment. i've called them 8 times and left messages. it is absolutely amazing and appalling to me that someone can seriously stay in business if they don't answer their damn phones. i probably will not be wasting my time with them.

when i visited the hospital on tuesday. feb. 18th, it was disgusting that antibacterial dispensers -- one in front of the au bon pain cafe and the other right near the main entrance next to the info desk -- were empty at a time when the us is trying to prevent a pandemic. particularly as people with compromised immune systems visit hospitals, but even in light of the hospital's simply being a place that is supposed to stop-- not spread -- infectious diseases -- this was surprising. however, more astonishing was that when i notified the woman working at the info desk that morning, she appeared uninterested. i then went to patient family services. two people-a young man and woman -- were  chatting behind a desk. when i explained that there was no antibacterial soap in main area of the hospital, they did nothing. i explained that it would be very helpful to fill the soap dispensers in the main area of the hospital right next to the front info desk as well as the dispenser that was in front of the au bon pain restaurant café.the young man named joel explained that when the custodian did his rounds, they would let him know. he did not know what time that would be, but it would be in the morning. this had nothing to do with keeping the hospital clean and  safe but everything to do with minimizing one's work for joel in the ambivalent young woman.  the young woman behind the desk who had been chatting with joel prior to the interruption of work giggled. i suggested that since dispensers were empty, that it would be good to call custodian services now to fill, but joel said he would not do that; the young woman was also ambivalent to act.

i called several offices. thinking that those whose job it was to take care of these issues were ambivalent, i asked the switchboard to connect me to secretary to the president. the  switchboard rep stated that these calls went to (the (ambivalent) patient services. meanwhile i saw many people trying to wash hands when entering the hospital and the restaurant -- only to find empty dispenser. i finally called the director of nursing, explain that i knew nurses cared-- and patty in that office was great.

but -- it is disgusting that the other staff members seemed to act -- or not act -- out of ignorance. i did wonder if such a basic step in patient care could not be taken, what happened with more complex issues. i have found care to usually be excellent at the hospital, but this was negligent. there was the same issue of empty dispensers at brigham's fish center. the hospital needs to get with its own program.

i had to come here for some labs, and i was very pleased at my experience. 

like any big complex, i had to find my way around, but people were very nice and helpful. the wait was very short, despite the fact that i had been sent here (along with i am sure many other patients) due to issues at another campus, so they were likely a little overloaded.

everything was clean; the staff was friendly and knowledgeable, the process was minimal.

this was also during the covid-19 epidemic, and they were screening anyone who came through the door to try and keep the facility uncontaminated, which while not perfect was a good gesture for sure.

i would happily come back here again in the future for other procedures based on the quality of service i received.

hopefully you read this before going to the er, not after like i did.  reading some of the other reviews - similar things happened to me.

on friday february 28th at about 8:30pm my daughter and i took our 18 month old grandson to the emergency room on bee ridge and cattlemen.  

1.  my daughter was holding the baby who was crying - he had been bitten on the hand by a dog.
2.  the security guard never looked up from his computer and mumbled for us to sit down - "they know you're here."  we were the only people in the er, so i'm thinking "who knows we're here?"
3.  three women were behind a desk and did not make eye contact with us - no concern for a young woman holding a crying baby.  they just talked to each other - nobody told us anything.
4.  five minutes becomes 10 minutes and nobody said anything to us.
5.  after about 10-12 minutes a door marked triage opens and some patient comes out.  the triage nurse asked us to come in.
6.  she did not wash her hands, use purell, or wear gloves.
7.  she had to do all the typing to get us into the system (i guess the other three women were busy not helping)
8.  after about 15 questions - she finally asked why we were here.  we told her he had been bitten by a dog.
9.  when she reached for his hand - he of course screamed - so she reached for an unsanitized teddy bear on her desk and gave that to him to quiet him down.
10.  she dabbed the wound clean (did not rinse it) and moved us through some double doors into another waiting room with about six chairs - again we were the only people there.
11.  about another 10-15 minutes later a nurse came in and confirmed the baby's name.  then she asked us if he had a fever?  no?  a cough?  no?  we told her he had a dog bite.  (i wonder why she hadn't read the triage report??)
12.  she asked my daughter a dozen questions which had nothing to do with the dog bite, including vaginal or c-section delivery?  i'm guessing that is a priority when treating a dog bite.
13.  another 10 - 15 minutes and a doctor came into the room.  and here's where i started to question this whole operation.  he never came closer than 10 feet from the baby - never looked at the wound, let alone cleaned it.  from 10 feet away he then described what he was going to do - he was going to order an x-ray and then give us some antibiotics - because he told us without antibiotics the risk of infection is very high.
14.  another 10-15 minutes and a guy from x-ray came and told us he had been instructed to an x-ray of the right hand.  "is this _____?"  good guess!

did you ever see the movie zootpia where she has to go to the dmv to get her license?  that's what this experience brought to my mind.  they were like the sloths but without the smile and the compassion.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drhsktakrzc 

15.  another 30 minutes and the nurse came back asking us what was happening.  that is when i got a little frustrated and asked her why the doctor had not even looked at the wound?  why hadn't the wound been cleaned?  she seemed to think that the doctor had looked at the wound.
16.  i could go on and on...

finally the nurse came back with the prescription for the antibiotic - it was now 11 at night.  i asked her if she could call in the prescription so it would be ready when we got there.  "we don't provide that service."

this is a perfect example of an organization which is driven by procedure - and has absolutely no focus on patients.  no compassion, no coordination, no communication.  the system these people work in has crushed their humanity - and this is with an empty er.

all the while i'm thinking to myself - "omg imagine if there was a corona virus outbreak in sarasota and there were five or six puking sick people in the er waiting room?  this hospital is completely unprepared to handle anything like that."

come to find out two days later that there was a corona virus patient in the hospital that night - and i thought back to the people not washing their hands, etc. etc.  i pray that my grandson, my daughter and i were not infected.  

and hannah b. don't respond "i am so sorry to hear about your experience..."  if you gave a damn, you would go to the er yourself and see what your customers see - it isn't pretty.  if you did care, it would either be fixed, or you wouldn't be working there.

i love sharp coronado hospital sewall healthy living center! it is like one stop shopping for helping me be the best i can be. it is all about patient centered care and helping you meet your needs. bob is a nurse practitioner and acupuncturist - he has helped me immensely me  with my varied issues and i love how warm, caring and professional he is while  providing the treatments.  cynthia is my personal trainer who is wonderful at helping me recover my strength and function after a bone fracture.  she looks at me for who and where i am in my health status, my age, my own wishes and individualizes  my exercise plan to help me gain the strength and agility to keep me on my feet .....and is nice while doing it!!

i was transferred here last wednesday @ 6am from hoag. i didn't start my care until 30 hours later, thursday. i brought with me multiple mri copies from the previous 24 hours at hoag/ private mri facility. not only were these discs lost, (2 separate times), but i was told they were uploaded to my patient portal. unfortunately this wasn't true because my doctor told me they were never uploaded. the discs were eventually recovered. this caused the 30 hour delay, as confirmation of mri results were needed to help expedite my care.

this minor frustration was easily overlooked, until i received a biopsy on my l4 spine, on thursday afternoon, the following day. the next 4 days have included doctors telling me the results aren't ready, or the doctors not coming by at all. until today, monday, my doctor finally informed me the hospital lost my biopsy cultures. 

my doctor was very upset as well because the last 4 days i was told we are waiting for the biopsy results to start my specific antibiotic care plan. well now they lost the biopsy cultures and since the biopsy was on my spine my doctor doesn't feel comfortable ordering another. instead, he says we will just treat the problem with pathology results.

so my bone cultures are lost. i've been recovering in the east tower. my mri discs were lost. (since recovered) and i still don't have an update from my case manager, regarding my outpatient care plan. 

again, the nursing staff have been extremely kind. (5 star for the nurses in east tower)

but, i am beyond disappointed with this current experience. a week in the hospital, with minimal progress. 

i will update accordingly.


- since i posted my review i was contacted by hospital administration and nurse lead. both were extremely kind and understanding of my situation. they are doing their best to resolve this situation so it doesn't happen in the future. again, i appreciate the nurses and staff during this stay. also, dr goldstein, did an excellent job of communicating directly. thank you fountain valley for helping remedy this situation, as all we can do is move forward!

review: i give this location 2 stars mainly because i was literally having a asthma attack i told the lady in the front , filled out the info i needed to and walked right to the triage . i'm literally wheezing and the nurses were asking me questions . i clearly stated i had asthma and they still didn't offer me oxygen ... my chest pain was a good 6 out of 10 . i never waited this long for oxygen ... i mean i was having an attack i should've been priority . meanwhile at least ten homeless people were in the waiting area stinking up the place . any who , another nurse kindly give me a mask with oxygen to then moments later ask me to walk to a different room (mind you i'm heavily wheezing) usually hospitals don't make you walk if you have respiratory issues ... i'm wheezing my way to the room to then start my treatment all over . it's crazy how a nurse had to ask more than once if i have asthma ... registration ppl are great and the doctor was awesome . but those nurses that check your blood pressure and heart rate . ignorant

not impressed at all. i was avoiding going to the er or the doctors. this was the sickest i had ever been in my life, but i had no fever and figured it would pass as it most likely was a virus. i was forced by my employer to go to the doctor to avoid occurrences. i was vomiting constantly non-stop for days on end. i couldn't keep anything down. i laid in bed and went from the bed to the bathroom vomiting. i was then vomiting blood. (probably from the non-stop vomiting and dry heaving for 4 days straight) i went to urgent care and couldn't walk or stand long as i felt like i was going to pass out and was very short of breath. i had to sit down every few steps. they stated they couldn't help me and to go to the er as i was severely dehydrated. because every time i stood up, my blood pressure would drop.
i went to the er and the idiot that brought me to the er bed was walking very fast and far. my husband was on her foot while i dragged behind and literally couldn't keep up and felt like i was going to pass out. i had to stop and called to my husband to please hold up. when i got to the bed, she looked at me in disgust and said she needed a urine sample. i hadn't peed in over a day as i had nothing to pee out. so i said, i couldn't pee as i haven't urinated in over a day. she looked at me, rolled her eyes and said, "then try!" then walked out of the room.
i was given an i.v. for fluids. while i was receiving fluids, i heard the nurses complaining about the patients and that they "treat them and then street them" as the patients were a pain.
seriously???
my step father (whom died a year ago) went here as he was bleeding out of his port badly. (he had renal failure) they took him in, they were unable to stop his bleeding, so they released him. he went to his practitioner and the practitioner was furious with geneva and had him go to f.f. thompson hospital where they were able to treat him and give him a blood transfusion.
about ten years ago, a friend's sister took her son here, as he was complaining that his stomach hurt badly and it had turned purple. (he was seen by a geneva practitioner and released, stating it was just a gastrointestinal bug) they went to geneva, the boy died under their care. he had peritonitis.
do not go here!!!

this hospital used to be wonderful. since being taken over by nyu it's abundantly clear that it's profits over patients. the hospital is over run with interns and residents. they don't even read your chart when they come into the room and you have to tell the same story over and over and over again. 3 of them will come in and want to take turns checking your already upset toddler. my daughter came in with a stomach virus with dehydration and low blood sugar. the interns and residents treated her symptoms but had zero regard for anything else i was telling them. they dismiss the mothers who know their babies best. the nurses, child life specialists and other staff were wonderful but the "doctors" in the pediatric unit are terrible. i was told they wouldn't run anymore tests because it's a waste of hospital resources.  i will never return to winthrop again.

how osha didn't shut down this hospital yet is beyond me. a nurse removed my iv without gloves, make matters worse. it was during the corona outbreak scare. i was laying in a hospital bed without a diagnosis but taking meds and had an iv in. so what was i being treated for when no one knew what my diagnosis was.

i had to ask, (two days later) what my diagnosis was and what i was being treated for.  finally, after much debate, they sent me for a ct scan which is the boilerplate basic protocol if you ask me. the medical professional school rejects from all walks of life work here. buyer beware! run!!! do not go here if you can help it.

hospital food is awful, worse when most of the food looks like something i wouldn't even feed my dog.

if i could give this hospital -10 i would had a very bad experience there with my son reluctantly had to go there with my husband even though i begged him to go to a different hospital. he had flu like symptoms oxygen level was in the 80s we had went to minute clinic in cvs and lincolnton. the nurse practitioner there was very nice but said because my husband's oxygen level was so low she had to call an ambulance for us we decline the ambulance but went straight to the er at atrium hospital.
  the people in the lobby of the er were very professional and kind got us in very quickly. and that's where the bad experience started. we were put in the room he was hooked up to machines to keep track of his vitals his oxygen kept dipping down into the 70s and 80s. the alarm for the o2 sensor kept going off because of the low oxygen we had to call the nurse several times to come in and she would just say it's a bad reading. they changed the monitor on his finger it was still reading low. they gave him a bag of fluids and blew out his vein in his arm then drew blood from his hand blew that vein also. when the doctor finally came in talk to him about the low o2 oxygen and he said it was probably faulty equipment to which i said is all your equipment here faulty because they had changed the sensor several times. at one point i put a timer on my phone to see how long it would take a nurse to come in with the alarms going off i stop my timer at five minutes and called the nurse and she said i know that is an annoying sound i'll shut it off i told them that i was more concerned about his oxygen being so low then the alarm is going off and asked if he could be put on an oxygen so they did his oxygen stats were  still low 90s even with being given oxygen. when the er doctor came in i asked him if he could be checked for the coronavirus because within the last week he had been to international airport. the doctor told me the coronavirus was not in north carolina to which i said well it wasn't in texas last week either but now it is. the doctor said he doesn't have the symptoms of the coronavirus to which i said he has all the symptoms of the coronavirus and they still would not test him they did not even test him for the flu. when they admitted him to observe him overnight the transport person almost ran him into several different objects for different times. we get to the room and the doctor that we had was very nice but still the test he ordered no one even did them he ordered a flu test they didn't do it he ordered a walking oxygen test they didn't do it. he had wanted him to be off oxygen for the night to see how he did he wanted it to be monitored they never took him off the oxygen and never monitored him with no oxygen. they said his oxygen was high enough to be able to go home and sent him home. he had only been off oxygen for one minute when they made that determination. very very very incompetent and very unprofessional

how can you truly rate a hospital? based off of skill of drs/surgeons/np/nurses/cnas? of quality of care? quality of food(which we all know who have been in a hospital for any extended time can be atrocious)? how about all of the above!

i was admitted on 11/7 for a major surgery. not simple by any means and i am glad and blessed that this was the hospital i went to. aortic valve replacement which entails open heart surgery is scary enough to hear, but the team here at sharp memorial along with my surgeon dr. adamson put my fears to rest. from the initial consultation with him and going over what was to occur i felt at ease along with my girlfriend. even making jokes with me to relax me and calm my nerves just showed the bedside manner was well above par.

the complex is large and if you have multiple appointments in different buildings as i did. just ask the nurse assisting you to request a shuttle and they will get you to were you need to go. instead of moving your car over and over and dealing with the parking.

depending on what you're in for will dictate what floor/building you will be placed in. post op recovery icu is 2nd floor of main building and god bless if that's what you're in for.

nursing staff along with the np(nurse practitioner, don't call them a dr even if they're right there) have some of the most gentle care i've experienced from any hospital. i've bee. to other sharps and i can wholeheartedly say this hospital takes the prize. from providing you with as much information as possible to assist you in your recovery to ensuring you help is merely a call away by providing you with their direct number(they're given a cell phone at work so they can be reached by you or the nurses station if needed urgently) these ladies and gentleman embody care. my hats off to floor 6 (cardiac recover) for all the outstanding service and care they provided me. i honestly don't think i would have been recovering as well as i am without their support and care.

food is still none the less hospital food but i was able to speak with the chef in charge and here their plans for the coming year. adopting a comprehensive plan to ensure that the food quality and nutritional value are in keeping with the care provided at the hospital. a one of a kind program that already has made staples in improving the quality of the food and nutritional value(small steps so far such as switching from iceberg lettuce to green leaf lettuce and such). my hats off to them for improving this overlooked aspect in hospitals. the ordering system is fantastic how they take your meal order ahead of time to not interfere with your recovery and to ensure that you designated meal with restrictions if any get to you on time. i lived how each .real came with a nutritional overview letting you k ow nutrients, calories, etc in your meal. loved that!

radiology/radiologist as i had to deal with frequently were friendly and helpful. whether they had to assist me in my room or take me down to get mris(be aware, its always the coldest part of the building because they do have to keep those machines cool or they can burnout so ask for bra blanket if you need it). the transport team who assisted you getting from location to location or helping you leave in the end were always kind, helpful and made sure you knew you were always welcomed back.... hopefully not soon though.

all in all if i could rate this hospital a 11 or higher i would! excellent is the only word i can come up with to describe the care provided by the staff at sharp memorial. my hats off to all the staff that help in the recovery of the many patients who walk through their doors and the supporting staff behind the scenes.

i am a rn with 22 years of experience, er included and this is the absolute worst that i have seen patients treated.  unfortunately two of my fellow nursing colleagues have been extremely rude and disrespectful to patients in the waiting room which is never acceptable even when they are a challenge.  a patient was told in the waiting room by one of the nurses that is she was unhappy that she could just leave.  just horrible!  not only for that patient but to all of us that witnessed the lack  of compassion and care.  a triage rn came out to make an announcement at 7:40 pm wearing a mask and got totally po when she was told that people could not  hear/understand her.  please consider having more supervision for your er team during the off shifts until the  staff can demonstrate proper care, consideration, respect, and customer service to the patients.  please do better.

i went into urgent care because getting an appointment with my regular physician would take a month and an available physician would be a week!

i could have died!

but fortunately, i was nowhere near death. what i thought was a possible urinary tract infection or kidney stones were both false. i evidently didn't know where my kidneys were. such a embarrassment and a fail. all my panicking where for nothing.

but with urgent care, i got my piece of mind and all i needed was aleve and a heat pad for my aching lumbar muscles.

i felt the staff who helped me were kind and the facility is clean. they supply hand-sanitizers everywhere and face mask, if you want extra protection from airborne illnesses. 

abundant amount of parking if you don't mind walking. the facility is huge!
fac_name: Kaiser Permanente Woodland Hills Medical Center

review:
i have been to this hospital several times over the years, in different units, when it was winthrop, during the nyu affiliation years, and recently post-nyu acquisition.  overall, i have had positive experiences.  care, staff, facility, etc.

the following is based on recent visit to the er.

background: busy flu season.  hospital had been on diversion recently.  ip beds full.  er very crowded.  placed in area outside main er.

first, the positives.  these er staff were excellent:

barry zou, rn (triage nurse) - awesome; demeanor, thoroughness
"mo", rn
s. datta, md
grace, rn
christine cirillo, rn
dr. lori katinas, md internist
eugene sullivan, do, gi = no ego; easy to talk with; gave us great ideas, hope
odette thomas, do, hospitalist medicine and her pa laura zaveski. - both so compassionate and patient-centered
n. hussain, do, endocrinology - easy to talk to; listened
tray - environmental/aid - great manner with patients, families, colleagues
firenze b - very understanding
ben, rn

management/professionalism:

felt like there was very little physician or rn oversight or presence in the er. no sense of leadership presence. this erodes patient/family confidence in staff ability to provide appropriate care, competently and timely.  this is heightened by fact that a lot of staff only a few years out of school.  

staff were observed discussing personal issues, staff-staff issues/gossip, other patients, vacation plans, "crazy people", etc.  discussing patients in areas where others (everyone) could hear.

staff need coaching: e.g., christopher d., rn - did not treat patients with respect and dignity (despite patients being challenging); i observed his demeanor with one challenging patient in particular; it is never ok for any staff member to be rude, argumentative, dismissive, and poke fun at a patient - or anyone for that matter; terrible. this rn threatened to withhold meds "next time i won't give it to you." laughing, rn said, "it's almost entertaining...you have to laugh at it" referring to the patient.  another rn had to take over caring for the patient.

lack of attention to patients - hours would go by w/out staff attending to a patient.  what is rounding protocol?

noisy - staff loud and boisterous in late evening and early morning hours - disruptive and not at all conducive to healing 

upon arrival to er check in - rn kelly wore mask but later had it pulled down below chin.  rn in nearby room celebrated he had just seen his "last patient" before his shift ends, but noted unfortunately he had to fill out some sort of paperwork; he held up a folder with a pink sheet of paper

masks - lackadaisical approach by many staff with respect to wearing flu mask - either pulled fully off face or wore half on - below nose.

musical chairs - patients left in chairs (not enough beds); moved several times within the same ancillary/accessory side area: why?

cramped spaces - er berths only as wide as a bed, with flimsy partitions that would not always stay in position.  very little (no) privacy.

providers (resident? and student) - using patient spouse for medical (clinical) translation to get medical history, document symptoms.  staff knew little or no spanish.

while the hospital was extremely busy (flu season), there is never any excuse for staff to act in the ways described.  this behavior is unsafe, provides a poor patient experience, and undercuts the work of team overall.  i encountered many (named above) excellent, caring team members.

i hope this feedback improves care and environment at nyu winthrop.  i want this hospital to thrive in our community.  we have much need for healthcare access.
fac_name: Emergency Department at NYU Winthrop Hospital

review:
went there in the afternoon on december 26. you fill out a piece of paper with basic information and then sit down. after a while you get called to a desk to be checked in. then you wait. there were people coughing all around the waiting area. there's a sign saying that people coughing should wear a mask, and where to get one, but nobody was. many of these people were morbidly obese. after i'd been there perhaps an hour, i realized that only two people had been called into the treatment area in that time and there were quite a few people who were there before me, so it would probably be many hours before i would be seen. at that point, i decided to leave and not wait any longer. i hope to never go back.

perhaps it's less busy at other times, but since the waiting area is large and there are three desks for checking people in, and dmh has closed several other expresscare locations, i think it's probably often as busy as when i was there.

eileen was very rude to my boyfriend .. he came in with some kind of a stomach virus and she tried to insinuate not once but twice that he was faking ... she said "oh you were fine before i came in the room" question for you eileen  ... we both work full time jobs just like u so  wtf would make u think we wanna be here at 7 a.m  on a saturday morning ... unprofessional ... your job is to make the patient feel better and comfortable but all u did was piss us off ... learn your place you work in service so act like it

took my son to the er the day before thanksgiving for having a 105 fever and they said he was fine they did a urine test, x-ray, and they swabbed for influenza they said nothing was wrong went back home again yesterday took him into the er at 1.30 am because he had a fever of 104.3 wen we went in they took his temperature and it was at 105.8 smfh they did blood work another swab for influenza and x-ray said the same fucking thing he's fine it might be a virus ... so they call my husband at 10pm tonight and tell him they reviewed his x-ray and it shows he has pneumonia they prescribed him antibiotics and my husband is picking them up tonight. like who the fuck misses the x-ray we went home at 6 am my son is 2 years old same thing happened last year. what if something worst happens to my son i read about seizures etc this is not fucking right they need to triple check everything they do. i'm so sad and mad whoever they got working in there obviously doesn't know what they're doing fucking idiots this is ridiculous

allegedly, my first review violated yelp's guidelines (this means someone who really cared must have flagged it) although my angered verbosity was very much provoked by a horrible experience i had with my mother getting checked into the er.  

without saying too many true words to stir the faint hearted, i felt that the er check in staff lacked professionalism and tact. interpersonal communication is a sensitive deal in that sector and yet we were treated like kooks crying over an inane issue.

apparently it's passé for a 64 year old woman to mysteriously collapse. i'm sorry you see the same thing over and over to the point you forget that you're dealing with other people's constant concerns over life and death. i'm usually a nice patron who realizes the soul sucking and overwhelming dread of customer service but how someone treads around my mom's life isn't innocently shrugged off like a bad cheeseburger. the 24/7 on-call nurse who determined my mom's collapse as an emergency made it seem like we were dealing with a seizure or a mini stroke so when we regurgitated her words to the guy at the er desk, he chuckled and condescendingly disregarded that information. people faint--yes. but fainting for a 64 year old with a family history of brain diseases can mask itself in a lot of alarming red herrings. just because you see "real emergencies" it doesn't warrant you to lose compassion and sensitivity. 

so kaiser, i hope i didn't violate anything this time by expressing that your er desk staff over on zion ave. really needs to have a pep talk about how to process patients with integrity and without making comments that are better left for a doctor to determine.

i was good as new on thanksgiving!  thank you both, including the warm staff at registration. 

i definitely would return!

review: horrible service! er nurse ivette was really rude! i do not like going to hospitals unless necessary. i have been sick for two weeks now. my primary doctor called me today and per cdc regulations she was told i should go to the er and get tests done. i followed her instructions and headed to gotlieb. i didn't expect them to test me for coronavirus. because obviously they need to rule everything else out first..... the nurse insisted that she didn't understand why my doctor would sent me there and said they couldn't do much for me. not just was she not careful when doing my swaps but she has a nasty attitude the whole time, acting like i was a bother. after waiting a while a provider came in to my room and i explained how rude her nurse had been and that i did not appreciate how harsh she did my swabs and the things she said. she apologized for the nurses attitude and insisted it was good that i went and that they would do the tests necessary. she left and the next person that visited me was the same nurse with her smirk face on to discharge me. they couldn't do anything for me and i should follow up with my primary health provider. she is a rude person and obviously in the wrong profession. also i understand that there is a lot going on with the whole virus thing but all i want is to go back to work!!!! and i need to do everything i'm asked to go back to work... our health system is failing and we need better service not this crappy hospital . next time i'll just go elsewhere never again

this is regarding the er. i was incredibly disappointed with the care received. my little sister fainted while in the shower during her period. she had a small gash on her head-- because it was on her face we wanted to make sure there was no scarring and thus took her to the er. when we got there, they checked us in... and called us to the back for an ekg and blood work (excessive, yes, but it is the er). they took us back to the front, and called us back again for a chest x-ray. the np was walking by so we inquired as to why a chest x-ray was needed for someone who fainted (with known cause) after an ekg was already done.  the np proceeded to tell us that football players have fainted and died (completely irrelevant). i asked her if the ekg was normal, and her response was that there was syncope and we needed to find the cause of the syncope. then she asked my 18 yr old sister if she felt a vagal response. i looked up what syncope was on my phone- "fainting"? why is a medical professional using these terms when talking to patients? terrible bedside manner. my sister had to ask what she meant, and she still was unable to explain properly. i asked if my sister needed all these tests as she has been acting completely normal- she just has a cut on her forehead and i wasn't sure if it'd scar. np asked when the fall occured and i told her it was 10 am (this was about 11 hours later), and she responded she didn't realize. i asked if they would give my sister treatment without all these diagnostics tests and the np said that they would not! we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor. 
the poor doctor came in a while later and was very sweet. i was ready to just have my sister receive treatment and leave, but my mother said it was important to tell/ask about what happened because other patients need protection to. i then went into detail of everything happened, and said i felt the chest x-ray was completely unnecessary, i was appalled that the blood pressure of a patient who came in because she fainted was taken after having a chest x ray, and the bedside manner and advanced terminology of the np (kim tarver) was unacceptable. very surprisingly, the doctor agreed. she professionally stated she agreed that the chest xray was unnecessary and my sister did not need a cat scan. she said the blood pressure thing was an outlier, but still needed to be noted...and she stated the terminology used was a personnel issue. after all this, she used liquid stitches (liquid skin) on my sister. she's good to go now, but it was an incredibly painful, unnecessary process.

i have been extremely sick for 2 days and knew i had the flu, so i called my doctor's office to see if they could call in a prescription for tamaflu for me. they said they dont do that, i would have to come in, and my regular doctor didnt have any openings so i had to see doctor dolan. fine. i will have my husband drive me and my 2 toddlers, who are all also sick but not as bad as me, to the appointment (because i am too sick to drive and we dont have a sitter).  so now we have 4 people sick with the flu in their waiting room. sounds great so far, right? way smarter than just calling in a prescription durning the middle of flu season, right? 

so the nurse calls me back, takes my vitals and swabs my nose for the flu virus. fine, whatever. then the doctor comes in and wants to know what i "want?". kind of weird thing to ask, but i tell her i think i have the flu and i would like tamaflu. she tells me i don't have a fever and i let her know i am taking dayquil religiously every 4 hours because i am very sick and it helps a little with the fevers. then she asks me how long i've had symptoms. i tell her and she says that's longer than 48 hours and they dont prescribe tamaflu after 48 hours. mind you, we are now at about 50 hours. i asked her why not, since i have read many times that tamaflu helps even if you start taking it after 48 hours. her answer was "it makes people nauseous". ok, i think that if that's your only concern you should let the patient make that decision. 

so after that conversation, dr. dolan says "your flu results will be done in a couple minutes". i told her i didnt see the point in waiting on the flu results because they wouldn't prescribe me medication anyway. all of the sudden she says that i might be a special case because i take steroids for an autoimmune disease that makes me more susceptible to pneumonia. 

at this point i'm wondering what's wrong with this woman. she goes on and on about how she wont give me tamaflu because it's been close 50 hours and it makes people nauseous, then literally her next sentence is telling me i'm a special case and i need to be on tamaflu.

anyway, she leaves for the lab results and guess what, i have flu type a. she gets my local pharmacy phone number to send over a prescription for tamaflu and i ask her for a prescription for cough medicine. she says they dont give prescriptions for that. fine. can you reccomend an over the counter cough medicine? "we reccomend a teaspoon of honey". i asked her to repeat herself because i was in disbelief. she repeated "a teaspoon of honey". listen lady, i already know you are a nut, but if you think i am getting up every 3 minutes in the night with coughing fits to eat a teaspoon of honey, not only will i not get any sleep but i will have diabetes by morning.

anyway, we head over to the pharmacy to pick up the tamaflu i had to suffer mind games at the hands of a doctor to get, and guess what. they didnt send my prescription to the pharmacy i specifically asked them too and gave them the number for. nope. they submitted it to my mail order pharmacy. so the kind people at the pharmacy called my doctor and told them to send over the prescription and cancel the order with the mail order pharmacy because my insurance wouldn't cover both. cool. except now i have to wait another half hour for my prescription. we wait a half hour, go back up, and they tell us my doctor cant seem to cancel my mail order prescription and they wont be able to do anything for me until the mail order is canceled. at this point i'm exhausted so we just leave.

as we get in the car to drive home my doctor's office calls to tell me what the pharmacy people already told me, that they sent the prescription to the wrong place and they were not able to fix it and i about lost my mind. they made a huge deal about how many hours i had been sick and didnt want to give me the medication, but then realized they should, but instead of sending it where they were supposed to, they sent it to mail order where it would take literally days to fill. i told them to cancel all the orders since "hours" seem to make a huge difference in efficacy. they had already wasted at least 2 additional hours at this point and i didnt even have the medicine yet. i just needed to rest and the stress was making me feel even worse.

done, right? nope, 2 hours later i get an email from the mail order pharmacy saying that my order will be delivered in 4 to 7 days. thanks dr. dolan and thanks to her super incompetent staff, i guess i will just wait and see if i get pneumonia.

oh, also, the staff at the doctor's office was apparently supposed to have me put on a mask so i wouldn't spread the flu virus to others in the waiting room with my horrible cough, and they didnt. doctor dolan told me that after she came into the examination room.

bye bye saint mary's! if this flu doesnt kill me i will be seeking care at another practice.

usually our emergency visits aren't too bad. the past two times i have gone have been a sh*t show. the first time (for an asthma attack) i bring my daughter in, we stand in triage for about 15 minutes waiting for someone to even acknowledge us. finally the nurse says he'll be with us soon. there's nowhere to sign in, and the window to be seen is closed. after standing there for 15 minutes another couple comes in, mind you were still standing there waiting for someone to at least take her name, the couple walks right in front of us into the triage area after the nurse had told us he'll be with us shortly. they are seen right away....we walked out.

that whole system they have is completely ridiculous and needs to be redone. out of respect for other patients and their privacy. 

most of the time the doctors and nurses are great, just depends on when you go i suppose.

this is going to personally be the hardest review i've ever written. it is with a sad yet grateful heart, that i commend the doctors, nurses, and technicians of inova childrens hospital. the people who work here have the kindest and most loving of demeanors, absolutely care about kids and their parents who worry so much, and i can't think of many places that truly are as loving as this place right here. i absolutely with five stars recommend this facility, and want to give the staff here the biggest possible shout out of support that i can. all of us human beings suffer the mammalian struggle, it's what we do that matters, and my hope is that you'll embrace each day and others on the journey. yes my oldest son was pronounced dead here. he had already died of a massive angelman syndrome related seizure, that triggered cardiac arrest at age five. it is the worst experience a parent can go through, and i don't want your sorrow, but if you could donate blood to your fellow humans that will help. the staff here that night kept me, from literally destroying everything as this is a living nightmare that took years to get through. never over. through.

before that my oldest went here for everything from the nasty rotavirus to seizures. multiple visits and my youngest has been here for respiratory issues. he's a bigger boy now, but guess where i'd go if he had a medical emergency. here. with love to all paramedics, i'm going to insist here. the doctors and nurses do everything they can, and honestly i have no idea how they work here everyday, as it definitely takes a special breed. it's a very clean facility, and getting in and out of here is relatively easy. also they don't forget who you are. it is a sad but wonderful circle of life, that on the night all was crushed, the same nurse who helped my oldest multiple times held on to his brother and loved on him. that as tear inducing as it is, that is a love of the highest i've ever seen. definitely you're in great hands here! while no parent wants their kid in the hospital, i recommend inova children's for everything.

so, i asked, if i were about to have a heart attack? or had been shot?

then, two 80 year olds who were reported as having fevers, who were actively coughing and who seemed weak, were brought in in wheelchairs.

review:
without a doubt, the worst er and hospital i have ever had the misfortune of setting foot in. my husband had a hernia with a bowel obstruction which could have easily lead to sepsis and death. he was in extreme pain, 9 out of 10, and vomiting.  he sat in the waiting room for over an hour for them to even perform the initial triage. even after the initial triage, it was another almost 2 hours before he was able to get back and get pain medicine.

the er doc was amazing, and probably did save his life. however getting him back there through the "system" was the issue.

even though he didn't have emergency surgery, because of his condition he was admitted. and it just went from bad to worse.

again, the doctors he did see such as the hospitalist and the surgeon and the er doctors were great. it was the nurses, the care (or lack therof), lack of communication, and the rest of the system.

even though i was recovering from the flu, they put him in a semi-private room and tried to move somebody in there with him. there were no masks available anywhere.  

i will be making reports to cms as well as to the florida quality review organization. i will never set foot in this hospital again and refuse to be taken there even if i'm dying.

review:
i visited the maternal fetal medicine clinic and was disturbed by the uncleanliness and overcrowding in the waiting room. chairs needed to be wiped down, there was a sick patient wearing a mask but was accompanied by three children and another adult. the waiting room is very small. the sick patient was not taken to another area. people were giving up seats to other arriving patients or waiting outside the clinic in the hall. also, several patients were taken  ahead of me even though they arrived very late for their appointments. we waited for nearly an hour to be called to the back. very unorganized and poorly managed. i was happy with the demeanor of the ultrasound tech who took care of us and the two minutes we spent with the doctor, she seemed nice.  the room we were taken to have the ultrasound was crammed with three chairs between the wall and patient bed. a third person definitely wouldn't be able to actually sit in the chair provided.
what's worse i woke up the following morning to a sore throat which progressed over the next couple of days into nasal congestion and a nasty cough that keeps me up at night.

mental health has some great staff (some not so great bordering negligent).  there's not much anyone can help with when they can only see you every couple weeks at the earliest...you'll be lucky if you get in one time a month.  that's 45 minutes of treatment for pretty significant complex chronic health conditions.  there's no "thrive" to be found here...its more like "dont die".  the staff is chronically on strike because the work conditions are horrendous.  mental health workers are typically compassionate people and it must eat at their core to see their patients treated so poorly and actually getting more sick while under their care.

another tip:  kaiser outsources all of their inpatient programs.  if admitted you and the uninsured of alamada county & contra costa will go to the same place and receive the same treatment.

review:
i brought my husband to this care station on december 26, 2019 because he was having flu like symptoms. we arrived at the care station at 1:30pm and was called in at 2:30pm. we were finally seen by a doctor around 3:15pm-3:30pm and he then proceeded to swab my husbands nose to get it tested for the flu. the dr. stated that we would have the results the following day because they needed to send the tube over to labcorp. i thought it was weird that they couldn't give the results right away being it's an urgent care but i left it alone and waited for the results. the very next day my husband wasn't feeling better so i called the care station at 10:14am to see if the results came in early and the 1st person that i spoke to stated that the dr. that saw my husband was in another location for the day and she would send him a message asking him to call us with the results. so we wait for 3 hours and i decided to call back again at 1:23pm and i speak to a 2nd person and she states the very same thing but what she did that the 1st person didn't do was state that she would have another dr. that's working in that office today call us with the results. she places the notice in his chart and apologizes. now we wait 3 more hours and 50 minutes, which makes it 5:13pm and i speak to a 3rd person and then she states his results are not in yet so you have to wait until the dr. calls. now i'm pissed because the last 2 people i spoke to stated that they couldn't give me the results and it has to come from the dr. which indicates to me that the test results are in not that they aren't in and a dr. has to give the results out and not them! she then process to tell me that this care station isn't an urgent care but a primary care provider and that the dr. would call us again. now lets remember what their website states "at care station medical group, our linden, nj walk in clinic is available to 7 days a week to treat your urgent care needs. we offer onsite labs, x-ray and ultrasound to quickly diagnose and treat you quickly so that you can get back to your busy life." regardless if this care station is a primary care provider or an urgent care the inconsistency that i got from 3 of the different people that i spoke too was not expectable! oh and to make matters worse today is december 28, 2019 and we still haven't received a phone call from any person at this care station giving us any results or at least calling us to state "i'm sorry the lab is probably backed up today which is why we haven't gotten the results yet or i'm sorry i know you called a few times today but i'll see what i can do for you on my end" etc. my husband is feeling worse by the minute and now i have to take him to a real facility that will actually provide him with the proper care and results that this facility stated that it would. since i was a teenage i've gone to this care station for several different reasons and the care has always been okay up until now! the flu is a serious virus that can kill people and i thought bringing my husband here would have benefited him but instead it did the complete opposite! i'm sad to say but if your looking for fast results and the proper care and treatment do not go to this facility!! you'll be wasting your time, money and effort! i truly hope someone here at this care station will read this review and never allow this to happen to another patient that is ill and in need of the proper care that you advertise. 

god bless

i would never expect five-star service from a government agency! (dmv anyone?)  so, i was blown away by the service i received from this clinic.  remember they're closed from 1130 am to 1 pm. i showed up precisely at 1 pm, and the doors opened promptly.   

you pay 50$ upfront for the consultation (insurance does not cover that).  within 15-20 minutes of arrival, my consultation began, and that included the time to fill out the paperwork. khanh gave me an excellent consultation; she broke down every city i was visiting in the philippines and told me every virus or outbreak that was currently happening in the region.

review:
an absolute horror show, travesty of medical care, and a lawsuit waiting to happen. 

my mom fell this week (fragile, dementia, history of stroke, and a hip replacement). i called 911 and on scene the paramedics asked which hospital we preferred- i chose mercy general as her pcp and records are all at dignity health. 

worst decision ever. 
how the hospital is run: 
a doctor saw my mom for a total of 1 minute at arrival and 30 seconds at exit. no supervision or accountability. lots of people here seemed "checked out" working in an untenable environment. 

medical assistants and one rn is on duty, one pa or doctor for what seemed to be 50 or more patients. there are lots of guys in green outfits doing, apparently, nothing that i noticed for the five hours we were there. my mom was parked on a gurney for the whole time in a busy hallway. people, patients, staff, gurneys, paramedics, security guards, and random people coming and going nonstop. 

she had imaging of her hip, elbow, and arm. there were good people doing the imaging. i repeated that her head hurt- mom chimed in- and then that was related to the doctor and a ct was ordered. too bad the doctor refused to talk to the patient and just felt  her bones for minute and didn't ask one question to her "patient" aka just a number.  props to the imaging team for maintaining a system and compassion for patients in a totally chaotic situation. 

she was offered a tylenol and glass of water. no updates on what was happening...i assumed a room would be provided eventually.  other patients parked in hallway, including a man and his wife- he begged to have someone help her use the restroom- for an hour. 

at about 8:30 pm the medical assistant popped by and said no broken bones, mom had to get up and prove she could walk before being released. i stepped in when mom got upright on the gurney and said she felt dizzy. 

medical assistant said she would have a chair behind mom as she walks. my dad was helping. honest to god, this was the plan. my mom fell, said she's dizzy, and they want her to walk in a busy hallway with people crashing around pell-mell. 

i spoke up loudly, said you need to get an orderly and she said, this is how we do it do you have a better suggestion? 

this could have been solved by having my mom move to a room- (literally across the hall an empty room with three hospital beds) for a safe environment for a trial run. 

we worked with situation at hand with me guarding the hall like a pit bull behind mom and blocking people and gurneys from coming through....and dad ready to catch mom. and then medical assistant tells mom to get back to 
the gurney after a successful trial run. mom has lymphedema and her swollen legs would be hitting metal. i said no get a wheelchair. then a guy in green shows up. apparently ready to catch mom if she falls. thanks, perfect timing. 

so, end of story- doctor comes by for 30 seconds to tell us no broken bones and runs off, totally masked  to protect herself from coronavirus. brava. medical assistant turned out to be a nice person and she stood by us while my dad got car. she was smart and empathetic once she was freed from caring for 50 people simultaneously with no tangible support. 

literally the worst er i have ever been in. train wreck, third world care. danger. no info. a few decent people trying to do their best in a disaster scene. never again. they should close their doors if they can't serve patients and provide a baseline of medical care. our east sac family has been born cared for. and died at mercy for three generations. sadly, switching care to sutter asap. 

every person who walks out of these doors should get a t-shirt that says, "i survived mercy er."

suggestion: hire some nuns to get this place shipshape. someone needs to be slapping a ruler.
